reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents a creator-run subscriber milestone giveaway offering a $100 Ulta gift card to a commenting subscriber. The announced winner is directed to contact the creator on Instagram and provide information for mailing the gift, but the described material shows no payment demand, credential request, or deceptive claim.

opening.argument: The promised reward is directly tied to viewer actions: the entry pool consists of people who commented and subscribed, and the selected person must contact the creator and provide information to receive the gift. That is a low-barrier reward-acquisition pathway, not merely a discussion of beauty products. The reward is presented as a $100 Ulta gift card, while participation and fulfillment depend on platform engagement and an external Instagram contact. This combination makes the solicitation itself the relevant conduct: viewers are encouraged to perform actions in exchange for an unusually easy-to-obtain monetary benefit.

citations.quote: Pick a random person who commented on my video they are subscribed to my channel
You have 24 hrs to DM me on IG so I can get your info to mail GM your gift
1K Giveaway|| $100 Gift card To Ulta

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling it a creator-run giveaway does not answer the central concern: the reward is conditional on commenting, subscribing, and then contacting the creator with information. The absence of an explicit payment demand does not establish that this reward-linked solicitation is harmless. Nor does naming a winner prove that the promised gift was actually delivered.

citations.quote: Pick a random person who commented on my video they are subscribed to my channel
You have 24 hrs to DM me on IG so I can get your info to mail GM your gift

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These quotes show an engagement-based giveaway and a winner-contact instruction, but they do not show a scam mechanism. They do not establish that viewers paid money, surrendered credentials, or were deceived; providing mailing information to receive a stated gift is not itself fraudulent. The title and spoken announcement identify the reward rather than proving it was fabricated.

citations.quote: the winner for the hundred dollar giveaway the youtube name is
it's a hundred dollars you can go to alta and buy your favorite makeup products

opening.argument: Several risk signals appear together: a $100 gift-card promise, an additional wallet, a 24-hour deadline, and a request to move the interaction to Instagram while supplying personal information. The offer is framed as an easy reward for ordinary engagement, and the deadline compresses the time available to question or verify the arrangement. Even if the speaker describes a selection process, the combination of a valuable gift-card claim and urgent external contact is consistent with a solicitation that can induce viewers to disclose information before independently confirming anything.

citations.quote: $100 Gift card To Ulta
You have 24 hrs to DM me on IG so I can get your info to mail GM your gift
i'm also going to send a hundred dollar. Wallet as well

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats each signal in isolation. It describes a valuable gift, a second item, an external Instagram handoff, and a strict 24-hour window, yet concludes there is no concern merely because the video does not say “pay.” Those facts support the opposite inference: urgency and information collection are part of how a reward solicitation can become deceptive, even without a stated fee.

citations.quote: You have 24 hrs to DM me on IG so I can get your info to mail GM your gift
i'm also going to send a hundred dollar. Wallet as well

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cited details establish only the terms of an ordinary prize claim: a deadline for the winner to contact the creator and information needed for mailing. They do not show that the deadline was designed to prevent verification, that the information was misused, or that the gift-card and wallet promises were false. Risk language cannot substitute for evidence of deception.

i have the receipt to it as. Well it's a hundred dollars

opening.argument: Although presented as a celebration of reaching 1,000 subscribers, the video functions as a promotion designed to steer viewers toward participation. The creator links the $100 reward to commenting and subscribing, asks the winner to move to Instagram and provide information, and separately encourages continued sharing and future engagement. The milestone framing makes the solicitation appear personal and trustworthy, but its operative message is still: perform platform actions and enter an external contact flow for a valuable reward.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The milestone story is not neutral context when it is used to drive more comments, subscriptions, sharing, and Instagram contact around a valuable reward. Describing the content as celebration overlooks its practical effect: it directs viewers into a participation pathway while building credibility through the creator's personal narrative. The promotional role is therefore central, not incidental.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The milestone framing explains why the creator is offering the giveaway; it does not conceal a separate commercial or fraudulent process. The engagement request is explicit, and the announced winner is identified. Those facts may make the video promotional, but the cited material still fails to show a deceptive claim, a payment request, or an unfulfilled outcome.
